html:
A council of bishops held in 410 at Seleucia-Ctesiphon, capital of the Sasanian Empire, that organised the Christians of Persia into one church. It became known as the Church of the East.

It met with the approval of Shah Yazdegerd I, who was friendly to Christians and on good terms with Rome. A Roman envoy, the bishop Marutha, brought the decisions of the First Council of Nicaea, and the synod adopted its creed. Isaac, bishop of Seleucia-Ctesiphon, was made head of all the Christians in the empire, with metropolitan bishops under him.

Being a church inside Rome's great rival, it soon claimed independence from the bishops of the Roman world, and later rejected the Council of Ephesus. That set it apart from Western and Greek Christianity. From Mesopotamia its monks and merchants carried the faith along the trade routes: to India, to Central Asia, and to China, where Alopen arrived in 635.
sum: A council of bishops held in 410 at Seleucia-Ctesiphon, capital of the Sasanian Empire, that organised the Christians of Persia into one church. It became known as the Church of the East.
